summary: Bambesa territory (Bas-Uele) lies far from the active conflict zones of eastern DRC and no armed group is reported to hold or contest territory there in 2025-2026. Recent regional security reporting concerns ADF incursions into Haut-Uele (Wamba, Watsa) and Ituri, several hundred km to the south-east, not Bambesa. Historical insecurity (LRA in the late 2000s, Mbororo herder tensions, poaching around Bili-Uele) has not translated into armed-group control. The main towns Dingila (GRID3 'Gbaka') and Bambesa centre (GRID3 'Embite') are administered and policed by the state; rural villages are assigned to the PNC by default state presence.

zones.description: Main towns: Dingila (GRID3 'Gbaka', Bambili HA) and Bambesa territory centre (GRID3 'Embite', Bambesa HA)
zones.evidence: Territorial seat and main trading town under state administration; no armed-group activity reported in Bambesa territory in 2025-2026 searches. Bas-Uele FARDC deployment described as thin, so the PNC is assumed to be the main day-to-day security force.

zones.description: Rural villages and small centres of Bambesa territory (Ganga, Titule, Kana, Zobia, Dembia, Makongo, Likandi, Lebo, Doromo areas)
zones.evidence: No reports of armed-group control in Ganga or Titule health zones; insecurity limited to banditry, poaching and periodic herder-farmer (Mbororo) tensions historically. State presence is sparse but uncontested; ADF activity in 2026 is in Haut-Uele/Ituri, far to the south-east.
